content:
Kenichi Takahashi (高橋 健一, *Takahashi Ken'ichi*) is a Japanese professional basketball player known for his career in the **B.League** (Japan's top professional basketball league) and his contributions to the Japanese national team. Here’s a detailed overview of his career and background:

---

### **Basic Information**
- **Full Name:** Kenichi Takahashi (高橋 健一)
- **Born:** March 13, 1985
- **Height:** 1.88 m (6 ft 2 in)
- **Weight:** ~85 kg (187 lbs)
- **Position:** Shooting Guard / Point Guard
- **Shooting Hand:** Right
- **Nickname:** "Ken" (ケン)

---

### **Early Life & Amateur Career**
- **High School:** Takahashi attended **Fukuoka University Ohori High School** (福岡大学附属大濠高等学校), a powerhouse in Japanese high school basketball. He led his team to multiple **All-Japan High School Championships (Winter Cup)** appearances.
- **University:** Played for **Fukuoka University** (2004–2008) in the **Kansai Student Basketball League**. He was a standout player, known for his scoring ability and leadership, helping his team compete at a high level.

---

### **Professional Career**
Takahashi has spent his entire professional career in Japan, primarily in the **B.League** (formerly the **NBL** and **bj-league** before the 2016 merger).

#### **Teams Played For:**
1. **Rizing Fukuoka (2008–2016)**
   - Joined the **bj-league** (Japan's now-defunct second division) in its inaugural season.
   - Became the **face of the franchise**, leading the team in scoring for multiple seasons.
   - **2012–13 Season:** Averaged **18.8 PPG**, 3.5 RPG, and 3.1 APG, earning **All-bj-league First Team** honors.
   - **2013–14 Season:** Led Rizing to the **bj-league Finals** (lost to Hamamatsu Higashimikawa Phoenix).
   - Known for his **clutch shooting** and **three-point accuracy** (career ~38% from deep in the bj-league).

2. **San-en NeoPhoenix (2016–2020)**
   - Moved to the **NBL** (later merged into the B.League) after the bj-league dissolved.
   - Played a key role as a veteran leader, helping the team transition into the new **B1 League** (top division).
   - **2017–18 Season:** Averaged **12.4 PPG**, 2.5 RPG, and 2.1 APG, shooting **40.3% from three**.
   - **2019–20 Season:** Helped San-en reach the **B.League Playoffs**.

3. **Shiga Lakes (2020–2022)**
   - Joined the **B2 League** (second division) team, providing experience and mentorship to younger players.
   - **2020–21 Season:** Averaged **11.5 PPG**, 2.3 RPG, and 2.0 APG.

4. **Fukuoka Rizing (2022–Present)**
   - Returned to his original team (now in the **B2 League**) as a **player-coach** in a mentorship role.
   - **2022–23 Season:** Played limited minutes but remained a respected veteran presence.

---

### **National Team Career**
- Takahashi was a **regular member of the Japanese national team** during the 2010s.
- **2011 FIBA Asia Championship (China):**
  - Averaged **10.4 PPG**, helping Japan finish **5th** (best result in years).
  - Key performer in Japan’s **79–78 upset over China** in the preliminary round.
- **2013 FIBA Asia Championship (Philippines):**
  - Averaged **9.8 PPG**, but Japan finished **9th**.
- **2014 Asian Games (Incheon):**
  - Played a supporting role as Japan won the **bronze medal** (first Asian Games medal since 1998).
- **2015 FIBA Asia Championship (China):**
  - Averaged **8.3 PPG**, but Japan failed to qualify for the **2016 Olympics**.
- **2017 FIBA Asia Cup (Lebanon):**
  - One of his last major tournaments with the national team.

---
### **Playing Style & Strengths**
- **Shooting:** Elite **three-point shooter** (career ~38–40% in his prime).
- **Clutch Performance:** Known for hitting big shots in critical moments.
- **Leadership:** Respected veteran who mentored younger players.
- **Versatility:** Could play both **SG and PG**, handling the ball when needed.
- **Defense:** Not a lockdown defender but smart and positionally sound.

---
### **Career Highlights & Awards**
- **bj-league All-First Team (2012–13)**
- **bj-league All-Star (Multiple selections, 2010–2015)**
- **bj-league Finals Appearance (2014)**
- **B.League Playoff Appearances (2018, 2020 with San-en)**
- **FIBA Asia Championship 5th Place (2011)**
- **Asian Games Bronze Medal (2014)**

---
### **Personal Life & Legacy**
- Takahashi is married and has children.
- Known for his **humble and professional demeanor**, earning respect from fans and teammates.
- After retiring (or transitioning to a coaching role), he is expected to remain in basketball as a **coach or front-office figure**.
- Considered one of the **best Japanese shooting guards of his generation**, alongside players like **Takuya Kawamura** and **Makoto Hiejima**.

---
### **Current Status (2024)**
- As of the **2023–24 season**, Takahashi is still listed as a **player-coach for Fukuoka Rizing** in the **B2 League**, though his playing time has reduced.
- He may officially retire soon to focus on coaching.

---
### **Fun Facts**
- Takahashi was **teammates with Yuta Tabuse** (first Japanese NBA player) on the national team.
- He once scored **40+ points in a bj-league game** (2012).
- Known for his **signature step-back three-pointer**.

---
### **Comparison to Other Japanese Guards**
| Player          | Height  | Position | Strengths                     | Era          |
|-----------------|---------|----------|-------------------------------|--------------|
| **Kenichi Takahashi** | 1.88m   | SG/PG    | Shooting, clutch plays        | 2008–2020s   |
| Takuya Kawamura | 1.93m   | SG       | Scoring, athleticism          | 2000s–2010s  |
| Makoto Hiejima  | 1.90m   | PG/SG    | Playmaking, defense           | 2010s–2020s  |
| Yuta Tabuse     | 1.73m   | PG       | Speed, NBA experience          | 2000s–2010s  |

---
### **Where to Watch Highlights**
- YouTube channels like **"B.League Official"** or **"bj-league Archives"** have clips.
- Search: **"Kenichi Takahashi highlights"** or **"高橋健一 ハイライト"**.

---
### **Final Thoughts**
Kenichi Takahashi was a **pioneer of modern Japanese basketball**, bridging the gap between the old **JBL era** and the new **B.League**. His **shooting, leadership, and longevity** made him a fan favorite, and his contributions to the national team helped raise Japan’s profile in Asian basketball. As he transitions into coaching, his impact on the next generation will be significant.
